title: Click-Delay Revisited
description: A while ago, I wrote a blog-post called The Curse Of The Click-Delay, on how to avoid the 300 ms click-delay on touch-devices, using a small JavaScript. Since then, iOS has been updated with a new CSS
body_html:
A while ago, I wrote a blog-post called The Curse Of The Click-Delay, on how to avoid the 300 ms click-delay on touch-devices, using a small JavaScript.

Since then, iOS has been updated with a new CSS-property:

touch-action: manipulation;

— and that property, along with some other settings, removes the delay without using JavaScript!

First, in the <head>-section, add either this:

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width">

— OR this:

<meta name="viewport" content="user-scalable=no">

You’re free to add more settings to these meta-values, like:

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, shrink-to-fit=no">

My updated CSS:

html {
  -webkit-tap-highlight-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0);
}

body {
  -webkit-touch-callout: none;
}

/* Elements with no delay, ie. button, label etc. */

button, label {
  touch-action: manipulation;
}

Happy coding!
